## 2. Print stream and bar kernel: dib_6000 on the _CANC print rule
Code: code/th_bars/kernels.py:97-147 `k_imb` (wmode 2, run 0) called at code/th_bars/build_month.py:114-118; print rule: autopilot/D8_PRINT_RULE.md sections 1 and 4.
1. Record side: from the book quote at the trade: last >= ask -> +1 (buy test first, so locked/crossed = buy); else last <= bid -> -1; else 0 (computed by me from /mnt/l2/l2vast/_bars/book, rows act = 84, `px >= apx`, `px <= bpx`). A record with missing bid/ask must be treated as 0 by NT8 (D8_PRINT_RULE.md 1, not met in the data).
2. Run merge ("print"): consecutive records of the same session with the SAME price and SAME side form one print; size = sum of sizes; no time condition; never across a session boundary (09:30 ET start, 12:00 ET end) or contract change. A print is stamped (known time) with the timestamp of the first record of the NEXT print (different price or side); the last print of a session: its own last record. (D8_PRINT_RULE.md 4 `_CANC`; verified by the rebuild below.) td 20261110 NY AM: 234,912 records -> 208,040 prints; td 20261027: 169,694 records -> 138,622 prints.
3. Kernel per print i (kernels.py:97-147), all state reset at each session key / instrument change (`eT=0.0` on key change): T0 = max(10, 6000 x s_n) prints (constant per trading date; s_n table in section 2b; build_month.py:118). w = price_ticks x 5 x size / 1e6 (wmode 2 branch: dollars of notional in millions with price in ticks: price points x 4 x 5); b = print side, if 0: +1 if price above the previous print's price, -1 if below, else the previous b (b starts +1 at session start). EWMAs (alpha = 1 / max(T0, 10)) updated for EVERY print BEFORE the test: ebw += alpha (b w - ebw), eabs += alpha (w - eabs) (init ebw 0, eabs 1); theta += b w (theta = 0 at bar open). Threshold = E[T] x max(|ebw|, eabs / sqrt(E[T])); the bar closes at the first print with |theta| >= threshold (>=). The closing print stays in the bar; o = first print price of the bar, h/l = extremes of print prices, c = closing print price; volume = sum of print sizes; n = number of PRINTS in the bar. After a close E[T] = 0.8 E[T] + 0.2 n, clamped to [0.25 T0, 4 T0]; E[T] starts = T0 at each session start. ebw / eabs are NOT reset between bars (only at the session start). Known time = the closing print's stamp. The open bar at session end is emitted with part = 1 (known = last record) and can never signal.
4. VERIFIED: rebuilt for both days from the tape with steps 1-3 (my code, kernel from th_bars): 214 / 325 bars, every column equal to the stored CANC bars (o, h, l, c, vol, n, known, part).
2b. Scales. **Day scales (how the per-day constant is built; identical code for every book of this page).** code/th_bars/build_month.py:13-32 `scales()`: for each trading date (td = ET + 6 h) the stats row of the 20 stats rows BEFORE that td (the current day is never used; values <= 0 dropped; at least 5 values, else the first-60-day median) are medianed; scale = that median / (median of the first 60 days). Columns: `rng` = daily range in points, built per UTC trade file, max over the pieces, / 4 (code/th_bars/stats.py:18; the quirk and the A/B holes are written out in autopilot/D8_ASIA_NEWBOOK_INPUTS.md section 2); `vol` = contracts of every record of the td; `n` = number of PRINTS of the td (run merge, same price and same tape side, never across a session code), table /mnt/l2/l2vast/_d8spec/runstats/stats_day.parquet. Checked here: for td 20261110 the runstats `n` = 463,946 = my own run count of the store tape (same price + same store side, break at session-code change): equal; the `_bars` stats_day.parquet holds the record count 530,480 instead (different column), so a coder must use the merged-print count for dib / tick rows.

## 3. Trigger: trig_levels_profile_va, variant break_native, n 2, k 0.25
Code: code/th_grid/triggers_d/lv_profile_va.py (line list), lv_base.py:23-45, fd_common.py:58 level_events (break branch :62-70), :20-37 lookup, :38-45 unit, :46-57 edge, :112-119 events_to_frame.
1. Series: one continuous series of all stored dib_6000 CANC bars (all sessions since 2023-04, sorted by known time); signal bar must be NY AM, part 0.
2. u (native, points) = rolling median of (high - low) of the previous 100 bars SHIFTED by one (bars j-100..j-1), min_periods 20, floor 0.5 (fd_common.py:38-45). k x u = 0.25 u. Example td 20261110: u 25.75 pt early, 19.25 at the last bar (INPUTS).
3. Lines (6, order): PRF1__POC, PRF1__VAH, PRF1__VAL (previous RTH day), PRF5__POC, PRF5__VAH, PRF5__VAL (5-day composite). Construction: section 4.
4. Level at bar j = line value at the last minute START <= T0_j = previous bar's known time in whole seconds; NaN if that minute is > 120 s older. Profile lines are valid from 18:00 ET of the evening before, so they exist at 09:30.
5. Per line: up_j = close_j > L_j + 0.25 u_j, dn_j = close_j < L_j - 0.25 u_j (each bar with its own L, u). LONG mask: up on bars j and j-1 AND close_{j-2} <= L_j + 0.25 u_j ("fresh": the bar before the hold was not beyond; compared with bar j's level and k u); SHORT mask: dn on j and j-1 AND close_{j-2} >= L_j - 0.25 u_j; then `edge` (mask False on bar j-1). Strict inequalities in up/dn, non-strict in the fresh test (fd_common.py:62-70).
6. OR over lines; first line in list order = fired; bar with both sides dropped. Break goes WITH the break (long above, short below).
VERIFIED: engine module = events file 10,318 / 10,318; my implementation on INPUTS gives the same signals (one parity-page timestamp slip, section 8).

## 4. Lines: construction and caveats
Code: code/th_grid/triggers_d/fd_profile.py:19-45 (`va`), :46-60 (histogram), :61-71 (composite), :72-86 (placement). Histogram of every NQ trade record of ET 09:30-16:00 of day d (ticks, volume = size, no merge). Value area: POC = argmax; expand from the POC taking the 2 rows above (hist[b+1:b+3]) versus the 2 rows below (hist[a-2:a]), the larger sum first (above if >=), until accumulated >= 70% of the total; VAH = top row b, VAL = bottom row a. PRF5 = the same on the summed histograms of the five latest AVAILABLE store days up to and including d. Day d's lines are used on the next trading date from 18:00 ET (td 20261110 uses ET day 20261109; td 20261027 uses 20261026).
VERIFIED: recomputed from the tape: td 20261027: PRF1 POC 29480.00, VAH 29571.00, VAL 29350.00; PRF5 POC 29500.00, VAH 29715.00, VAL 28991.50; td 20261110: PRF1 POC 27940.00, VAH 28095.50, VAL 27799.50; PRF5 POC 29561.25, VAH 29677.00, VAL 27246.75: all equal to the INPUTS (< 0.01).
**PRF5 hole.** The engine store lacks days 20261102-04, so the td 20261110 composite = ET days 1029, 1030, 1105, 1106, 1109 (that is why PRF5 POC is 29561 while price is ~27,900). A hole-filled composite (days 1103, 1104, 1105, 1106, 1109 from hist_replica; FORMULA, same functions, not an engine run) gives PRF5 POC 28320.00, VAH 28969.00, VAL 27221.50. Which rule NT8 copies (five latest available store days vs five latest calendar days) is a lead decision; the signals of td 20261110 that fire on PRF5 lines would change. td 20261125: days 1118-1124 not in the engine store (NOT verified).
Data NT8 needs: volume-at-price of ET 09:30-16:00 for the last five RTH days.

## 5. Bracket, sides, window, one position
- Bracket: stop 60.0 pts and target 60.0 pts from the entry fill, fixed, 1 lot (plain60/60 cell bracket; no unit rule for this book).
- Sides both; window NY AM code 3, part 0; scheduled exit 12:00 ET + 1 s.
- Two dib bars can close in the same second (e.g. 14:37:14.054, 14:37:14.893, 14:37:14.914 on 1110); the engine event time is floor + 2 s so two signals of one side in the same second give the same event time; the one-position rule handles it.
**Signal to engine event (VERIFIED in code).** Event time `ts` = floor(known time of the signal bar to whole seconds) + 2 s (code/th_nyeng/ny_build.py:32; code/th_brkt/brkt_build.py:42); events with ts >= the session-end instant are dropped (ny_build.py:33, brkt_build.py:46); session-end instant = the next ET session boundary after the signal bar (code/th_swap/common.py:32-40; for NY AM = 12:00 ET); the exit cap (N = 120 s, code/th_fakefill/cap_exit.py:9,20) is applied to the event file. Only bars with session code 3 (ET 09:30-12:00; code/th_swap/common.py:41-44) and `part` = 0 (not the truncated last bar of a session) can signal (ny_build.py:29; brkt_build.py:38-39). Sample-day checks: my re-run of the engine module on the stored bars gives the engine events file exactly for both sample days (counts below) and over the whole history (counts below).
**One-position / fill / exits (SPEC text copied from autopilot/D8_BUILD_SPEC.md block (b2), simulator code/replica/sim.py: NOT re-verified here).** MARKET order sent at event time; filled 1.0 s later (LAT_FILL) walking the 10-level book (buy at the ask side, sell at the bid side); stop = stop order at fill -/+ stop_pts (triggered by a print at/through the level, then market order walking the book), target = resting limit at fill +/- tgt_pts; ONE position per book: an event while the book is in a trade, an exit is pending or an entry is in flight is dropped (the next event after the exit is traded); scheduled session-end exit at 12:00 ET + 1.0 s (if no print follows within 120 s the exit is the last print before it); contract roll: flat 1 ns before the roll second, entries skipped roll-120 s to roll+300 s. Sizes: 1 lot per book in the engine runs (bare R0 base set; no stack rules in the TRADES blocks).

## Relay questions 2026-11-24 21:25Z (answers from engine code, read-only)
- Q5a LVN rule = LOWEST smoothed value, not depth against neighbouring maxima: code/th_grid/triggers_d/fd_profile.py `levels`: candidates i in range(max(a,1), min(b,len(sm)-2)) (a = VAL row, b = VAH row; range end exclusive, so the VAH row itself is out) with sm[i] <= sm[i-1] and sm[i] < sm[i+1]; `sorted(tr, key=lambda i: sm[i])[:2]` = the two lowest smoothed values (Python sort is stable: equal values keep the lower row first). A plateau gives its FIRST (lowest) row for LVN (<= left, < right); for HVN (sm[i] >= sm[i-1] and sm[i] > sm[i+1], i in range(1,len-1), |i-POC| > 8 rows) a plateau gives its LAST row; HVN sorted by -sm, stable.
- Q5b Kernel: k = exp(-0.5*(arange(-24,25)/8)**2), 49 taps, normalised by its own full sum, `np.convolve(hist, k/k.sum(), 'same')` over the histogram from the lowest traded tick to the highest (zero padding at both ends, output length = len(hist), centred). Matches the relay's sigma 8, +-24, normalised, zero padding. Histogram rows = every RTH record (ET 09:30-16:00) price in ticks weighted by size, no run merge.
